title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
summary: Given an integer array prices where prices[i] represents the price of a stock on the ith day, determine the maximum profit you can achieve by buying and selling the stock on different days.
statement: Given an integer array prices where prices[i] represents the price of a stock on the ith day, determine the maximum profit you can achieve by buying and selling the stock on different days. You can hold at most one share of the stock at a time, and you can perform multiple transactions (buying and selling) on the same day, but you must ensure you never hold more than one share of the stock at any given time.
constraints: Make any number of transactions while holding at most one share. Selling and buying again on the same day is allowed; doing nothing earns zero.
reference_solution:
def stock_profit_unlimited(prices):
    return sum(max(0, prices[i] - prices[i - 1]) for i in range(1, len(prices)))
hints: With no transaction cap or fee, separated rises can be collected independently.
Sum positive differences between consecutive days.
For each adjacent pair add after-before only if after is greater; otherwise add zero.
A long increasing run telescopes to its last price minus its first, so this does not require holding multiple shares.
editorial: Collect every positive adjacent change and ignore negative changes. Consecutive positive changes telescope into one buy-low/sell-high trade, and a sell followed by a buy on the same day is permitted. No feasible one-share strategy benefits from holding across an avoidable decline, so this total is optimal. The oracle exhausts all buy, sell, and wait choices on short price histories rather than using this greedy identity.

tests.explanation: Buy at 1 and sell at 5 for 4, then buy at 3 and sell at 6 for 3; total profit is 7.
Holding from 1 to 5 earns 4, the same as collecting the four consecutive rises.
